builder_plan.scenario: A support or data assistant repeats work across related customer requests.
builder_plan.change: Try the paper's memory change in a replay of past tasks, with separate memory per customer.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current memory pipeline plus a no-memory control using the same agent.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Task success, stale memories, retrieval misses, response latency, and all memory maintenance costs.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Diagnosing and Mitigating Long-Session Degradation in Full-Duplex Speech Models
summary: TRC replaces uniform full-detail retention of the entire conversation history in the KV cache with full-resolution storage of recent turns plus compressed key-value summaries of older history, paired with a lightweight self-distillation LoRA fine-tune to stabilize long sessions. It costs an additional LoRA training run with self-generated distillation data, architectural modification to the model's context handling, and some loss of fidelity for older conversation content. It can fail when older context is needed verbatim (the compression is lossy), when the self-distillation data does not cover the degradation modes of the deployment domain, and on architectures whose full-duplex streaming design is incompatible with the TRC cache layout.
rationale: If the reader operates full-duplex speech models in long sessions, the LoRA component is feasible on a single 24 GB GPU and the KV savings directly address memory limits, but both gains are validated only on three specific open models, so workload-specific testing is required before production adoption.
technique: Self-distillation LoRA plus two-resolution context compression

claims.statement: TRC replaces uniform full-detail retention of the entire conversation history in the KV cache with full-resolution storage of recent turns plus compressed key-value summaries of older history, paired with a lightweight self-distillation LoRA fine-tune to stabilize long sessions. It costs an additional LoRA training run with self-generated distillation data, architectural modification to the model's context handling, and some loss of fidelity for older conversation content. It can fail when older context is needed verbatim (the compression is lossy), when the self-distillation data does not cover the degradation modes of the deployment domain, and on architectures whose full-duplex streaming design is incompatible with the TRC cache layout.

LoRA adaptation mitigates degradation over ten-minute sessions across three full-duplex models, and adding the two-resolution context (TRC) architecture extends gains beyond the training session length while reducing KV-cache growth by more than 90%.
